Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-25

Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Asha Reddy (Redwood Product), Priya Shah (Halo Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (Halo ML Eng), Marcel Voss (Halo Security), Sofia Li (PM)

Summary: Quick intro, short qualification, 30m demo of JSON Mode + Console sandbox showing schema enforcement, safe tool invocation and runtime fallbacks, then pilot scoping and operational questions (VPC/KMS/SAML).

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Lena from Redwood. We have Marco our SE and Asha on product, can you wave Marco?
[00:08] Marco: Hey hi, good to see you all.
[00:10] Priya: Thanks, Priya Shah here, Head of Platform at Halo. We've been poking at inference runtimes and want to see how Redwood's structured output + tool invocation can fit into our routing layer.
[00:20] Lena: Great. Quick agenda: 10m qualification, 30m demo + console, 10m pilot scoping. Sound good?
[00:26] Priya: Yep.
[00:28] Sofia: Works for us.

[00:35] Marco: Alright i'll kick off with a quick overview of JSON Mode. The idea is we provide a first-class contract—so you give us a JSON Schema or OpenAPI-ish payload and the runtime will enforce types, run a validation step and optionally sandbox tool calls. Typical flow is: user prompt -> model generates typed payload -> runtime validates -> if there are tool calls we do a safe invoke through the sandbox or configured service.
[01:05] Ethan: When you say sandbox, is that in the hosted plane or can it live inside our VPC?
[01:12] Marco: Good question. We support both: hosted sandbox for quick evals and a VPC/private deployment where the sandbox runs inside your network and calls your internal services via secure routes. For pilots we usually start with hosted sandbox but you can push to VPC for security review.
[01:27] Marcel: How do you handle secrets / KMS for calls made from the runtime to our services?
[01:33] Asha: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and in Private deployments keys remain customer-controlled. For hosted we encrypt with per-customer keys and we can rotate keys on demand, also we log key use in audit logs. We'll follow up with the exact KMS flows in the SOC2 docs.

[02:05] Speaker 2: (overlap) ok cool.
[02:10] Marco: i'll share my screen and show the console.
[02:15] [screen share starts]
[02:20] Marco: Here is the console org for Halo's sandbox we pre-provisioned. Top-left you can see the JSON Mode tab, and i uploaded a schema for a vehicle-status action that your fleet UI needs.
[02:34] Priya: That's the schema we prototyped, yeah. We want strict typed responses because our downstream autopipelines rely on valid fields.
[02:42] Marco: Exactly. So i'll run an example prompt that triggers a tool call to your vehicle telemetry service. Notice the runtime will not let the tool call happen if the payload fails validation — that's the guardrail.
[02:57] [typing sounds]
[03:05] Marco: Ok executing. (slight pause) The model returns a typed JSON, validated, and then we show a dry-run in the console where you can inspect the generated payload and the proposed service call.
[03:20] Ethan: How do you protect against malicious prompts that try to exfiltrate PII or call destructive endpoints?
[03:28] Marco: Two layers — schema enforcement (so fields like admin_override must be boolean and we can whitelist allowed endpoints), plus runtime safe-invoke which maps logical tools to pre-configured adapters that validate parameter ranges, and we run a pre-invoke policy check. For extra safety in private deployments you can require manual approval during early pilot.
[03:48] Lena: Also worth noting we support response patching and fallback models. If the top model returns invalid JSON we can attempt auto-correction using a validation-guided re-prompt, or fall back to a smaller verified model variant to keep latency predictable.

[04:15] Sofia: latency is a big requirement for our UI. Need p95 under 400ms for short calls. Do you see that with JSON Mode + tool calls?
[04:25] Marco: It depends on whether a tool call requires external I/O. For pure-generation typed outputs we often hit p95 ~150-250ms on our hosted tier for short sequences. If there's a synchronous backend call we add network time. We can show you benchmark runs during the lab. We also use prefix caching and KV cache for repeated contexts to reduce tokens.
[04:48] Ethan: Can we quantize models to reduce cost on Dedicated?
[04:52] Asha: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles by workload. For pilot we can run a cost vs latency sweep and suggest an optimal q8/q4 profile.

[05:10] Marco: Now i'll demo tool function calling. I have two tools wired: vehicle-telemetry.getStatus and fleet-ops.scheduleMaintenance. We'll trigger getStatus first.
[05:22] [console click noise]
[05:27] Marco: The model generates the structured payload {"vehicle_id": "HALO-0421", "check_items": ["battery","brakes"]} — in the console that payload is validated and then we simulate the HTTP adapter call. The console shows the raw request/response and a replay mode.
[05:45] Priya: Nice — can that replay be scrubbed for logs? We need to avoid storing VINs in logs for 90 days.
[05:53] Marco: Yes you can configure retention and redact fields in the audit logs. We support field-level redaction and tokenization before storage.

[06:12] Ethan: If the model tries to call an endpoint not whitelisted, what happens?
[06:15] Marco: We block it and surface an error in the console. The policy engine is configurable — you can map logical tool names to your internal endpoint URLs only. The runtime never executes arbitrary URLs.

[06:30] [time jump, demo continues]
[06:32] Marco: Next: fallback orchestration. In this example i intentionally return an invalid float for battery level. The runtime detects schema mismatch and attempts a validator-driven re-prompt. If that fails we return a structured error payload and a recommended remediation action to the application.
[07:02] Priya: Will the client app get both the error payload and a human-readable message?
[07:07] Marco: Yes, you can configure the response envelope: structured error fields, plus a friendly message. We also provide trace ids so you can link to the audit log for debugging.

[07:25] Marcel: On compliance — for Private deployments do you provide certification artifacts? Our security team will need SOC2 and penetration test reports and an architecture diagram for our legal.
[07:36] Lena: Absolutely — we'll share our SOC2 attestation, and we maintain a redwood-private-deploy checklist that covers network diagrams, KMS integration, RBAC, and expected logs. I'll drop links after the call.

[07:55] Marco: A quick note about the tool sandbox: when in hosted mode we run invocations in an isolated worker with strict timeouts and per-tenant network policies. In VPC the sandbox runs as a local adaptor that you manage; calls never exit your network unless you route them.

[08:20] Ethan: For the pilot we want a canary that hits 5% traffic with auto fallback to our current microservice if anything fails. Do you support canary routing?
[08:29] Marco: Yes, canary + automatic fallback is supported by route policies. You can pin the model, define success metrics (error-rate, latency), and rollback rules. Console shows the rollout and health indicators.

[08:45] [screen switch to Optimize tab]
[08:50] Asha: Here you'll see Optimize's suggestions: batching thresholds, suggested prompt trims, and quantization recommendations estimated cost delta. For this workload it suggests enabling KV prefix caching for repeated vehicles which could save ~30% tokens.
[09:10] Priya: Can Optimize produce concrete cost numbers we can plug into our forecasts?
[09:14] Asha: Yes, we generate a token-level and model-level cost breakdown. For pilots we produce a forecast spreadsheet.

[09:30] Marco: i'll do one last live scenario: user asks for maintenance ETA, model responds with an action payload to scheduleMaintenance. The runtime will validate the schedule window and then call the adapter. You can require a manual approval step — here's the approval UI where an operator can accept or reject.
[09:54] Sofia: That's useful while we ramp.

[10:02] [demo ends]
[10:05] Lena: Ok quick qualification wrap: Priya, can you share your constraints? timeline? stakeholders?
[10:12] Priya: We're running a Q4 feature push; ideally pilot starts mid-Oct, production by end of Nov. Stakeholders: Platform (me), Security (Marcel), Fleet PM (Sofia), and the ML team (Ethan). Success metric: schema-valid responses for 98% of calls and p95 latency under 400ms. Budget is flexible but we need a cost forecast.
[10:37] Lena: Sounds doable. For pilot scope we normally do a 4-week sandbox with: schema enforcement on 1-2 endpoints, bench runs with 10k simulated calls, and an on-prem/VPC checklist. We'll provide pricing for hosted sandbox and for Dedicated/VPC.
[10:54] Priya: Good. A few security questions: can we enforce SAML SSO for console access, and do you support RBAC sync with our IdP?
[11:03] Marco: Yes SAML/SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported; RBAC roles map to per-org and per-route permissions. We'll supply the SAML metadata and a quick start doc.
[11:15] Marcel: Also need a clarifying point on logs — do you keep full request bodies in any long-term store for hosted? We prefer short retention with redaction.
[11:24] Asha: Hosted defaults to 30 days retention with optional field redaction. In Private we can set retention to your policy and not store any PII.

[11:40] Ethan: For the lab benchmark you mentioned — what telemetry do you need?
[11:44] Marco: We need a representative prompt set, expected sequence lengths, and a sample of parallel concurrent sessions. If you can provide 500-1k sample prompts and a target TPS we can run a qps sweep.

[12:05] Sofia: Ok we'll collate that.

[12:10] Lena: Alright let's recap next steps — Marco will provision the sandbox org and test tokens, i'll email pilot scope and pricing, Marco will coordinate the benchmark dates, Marcel will send KMS and encryption questions to the shared doc.
[12:26] Priya: Quick ask — can we get a short video clip of the console flow for our execs?
[12:31] Marco: Yep we'll record a 3-4 minute clip and drop it in the drive link.

[12:40] Lena: Final Qs?
[12:42] Marcel: None from me, thanks.
[12:44] Priya: No other questions.
[12:46] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the scope doc.
[12:50] [call ends]
